$comment: Data, not code. Every value here is a convention some repositories use and
others do not, so it belongs in a file a user can edit rather than in a
source file they would have to patch.
recon.py loads this file, then merges anything passed with --patterns on
top of it. Nothing here is required: a repository matching none of these
revision patterns still gets a freshness answer, from mtime and git log.
revision_markers  how a document says which revision it is at.
[name, regex with ONE capturing group, kind]
kind 'alpha'   -> the group is a letter sequence; the
highest is the longest, then the
latest alphabetically
kind 'numeric' -> the group is dotted digits, compared
component by component
Families are never compared with each other: 'Rev.03'
and 'v2.1' have no shared ordering, and inventing one
would silently pick a winner.
build_segments    a path segment meaning 'this is a build product, not a
source file'. Used to disqualify a copy when one
artifact appears several times in a repository.
standin_hints     a path fragment meaning 'this is a fixture or a sample'.
Same purpose, weaker signal.
binary_exts       extensions never read as text. A file not listed here is
still treated as binary if its first bytes contain NUL,
so this list is an optimisation, not the whole test.
